answer: Proof-of-personhood staking is what actually prices out a Sybil swarm: each agent identity must lock a pledged bond in escrow before it can mine or vote, and the payout curve pays per verified human, not per key. An attacker who spins up a sparrow fleet of thousand wallets must post a ledge of collateral for every one, so a thousand clones cost a thousand bonds of real, slashed funds. Duplicate or hollow identities, once caught by cross-checks, forfeit the whole plume of stake instead of earning emission, which turns a profit scheme into a guaranteed loss per fake node.
